stem: A recipient's grandchild receives a routine live-virus childhood vaccine. What infection-prevention teaching should the coordinator provide the recipient household?

options.text: Avoid contact with family members who received a live-virus vaccine within the past 2 weeks
No precautions are needed because live vaccines cannot shed after administration
Recipients should receive the same live-virus vaccine immediately at home
Permanently isolate the recipient from all children regardless of vaccination status

explanation.rationale_correct: Post-transplant infection-prevention teaching includes avoiding contact with family members who have had a live-virus vaccine within 2 weeks because shedding may continue for days to months.

rationale_incorrect.B: Live-virus vaccine shedding may continue for days, weeks, or months depending on the vaccine and host factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Live-virus vaccines are contraindicated after transplantation; household precautions are used instead.
rationale_incorrect.D: Teaching specifies temporary avoidance after recent live-virus vaccination, not permanent isolation from all children.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Avoid contact with family members who have had live virus vaccine within 2 weeks

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance after transplantation → ii. (avoid contact with family members after live-virus vaccination within 2 weeks); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 010600 item; live-virus household-contact angle distinct from infection-prevention combo (cctc-1024) and HPV teaching (cctc-1036); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: During long-term post-transplant education, a recipient asks how to protect bone health while on immunosuppression. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Exercise, and calcium and vitamin D supplements as indicated
Complete bed rest to prevent all bone stress
Stop all immunosuppression to reverse bone loss without medical guidance
Bone health requires no monitoring after the first postoperative week

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term immunosuppression teaching for osteopenia or osteoporosis includes exercise to slow bone loss and may require medication, calcium, and vitamin D supplements.

rationale_incorrect.B: Exercise is recommended to slow bone loss rather than complete immobilization.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bone health is managed with exercise and supplements under team guidance, not unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Bone health monitoring and counseling continue beyond the first postoperative week.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → j. Long-term effects → v.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Exercise recommended to slow bone loss … calcium and vitamin D supplements

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → j. Long-term effects of immunosuppression → v. Osteopenia or osteoporosis (exercise, calcium, vitamin D); PDF p. 120 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: A coordinator is revising post-transplant vaccination teaching materials. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Varicella and herpes zoster vaccines are contraindicated after transplantation.
Annual influenza vaccine should use the inactivated formulation.
Live herpes zoster vaccine should be given routinely to all recipients immediately after transplant.
Recipients should avoid contact with family members who received a live-virus vaccine within 2 weeks.

explanation.rationale_correct: Post-transplant vaccination teaching includes inactivated annual influenza vaccine, contraindication of live varicella and zoster vaccines, and temporary avoidance of contact with recently live-vaccinated family members. Live zoster vaccine is not routinely given after transplant.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—household contact precautions after live-virus vaccination are part of teaching.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and IV are also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; live zoster vaccine is contraindicated after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Varicella and herpes zoster vaccines are contraindicated … Annual influenza vaccine (not the live vaccine option) … Avoid contact with family members who have had live virus vaccine within 2 weeks

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance after transplantation → ii. (inactivated influenza, live varicella/zoster contraindicated, household live-vaccine contact precautions); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Synthesized item. Ninth complex_combo in bank; distinct from infection-prevention combo (cctc-1024); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A recipient and partner ask when sexual activity may resume after transplant. Which teaching aligns with standard post-discharge education?

options.text: Resume when comfortable unless otherwise contraindicated
Sexual activity is permanently prohibited after any transplant
Resume only after five years without any team discussion
Partners never need information about sexual activity after transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Sexual health teaching notes that recipients and partners want information regarding sexual activity and may typically resume when comfortable unless otherwise contraindicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sexual activity is not permanently prohibited for all recipients; timing depends on recovery and medical guidance.
rationale_incorrect.C: Resumption is based on comfort and clinical status rather than an automatic five-year delay.
rationale_incorrect.D: Partners are included in sexual-health education rather than excluded from information.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → j. Long-term effects → k. Sexual health → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Typically may resume sexual activity when they are comfortable in doing so, unless otherwise contraindicated

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → j. Long-term effects of immunosuppression → k. Sexual health → ii. (resume sexual activity when comfortable unless contraindicated); PDF p. 120 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
